thread:
maria-s: FYI customer AcmePayments reporting 401s after key rotation. They say rotation in Azure Key Vault succeeded but app still getting invalid_api_key from our API.

support-bot: Received customer ticket #C-12458. Tagging infra & eng.

alexg: Can you paste the exact request headers they're sending (redact key)? Often it's either wrong header name or hidden chars.

maria-s: Here's what they sent (redacted):

  curl -i -H "Authorization: Api-Key REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

They say they use Azure Managed Identity to pull new secret from Key Vault and atomically swap. Rotation time ~2025-11-03T08:12Z.

infra-az: A couple of things to check: 1) are they using Authorization vs x-api-key? our validator accepts both but proxy layers sometimes strip Authorization. 2) MSI libraries cache tokens locally for nontrivial TTL. If their process didn't refresh the env var after rotation, old key will keep being sent.

eli: Also check for LB or edge caching. We've seen customers with a sidecar that injects header and doesn't reload config.

maria-s: They confirm they use Authorization header and an internal sidecar (service-mesh). They did a secret rotate in Key Vault and updated a k8s secret, but the deployment is a long‑running Node process that reads the secret at startup.

alexg: That explains it. If process only reads secret at boot, rotation in Vault + k8s secret won't affect the running process until restart. Ask them to: 1) restart one pod to confirm; 2) dump the header value from the running process (console log) to check for trailing newline or invisible char.

maria-s: Sent repro steps to customer asking for a single-pod restart and to do `curl -v` to log raw request.

customer (reply via ticket): Restarted one instance, still 401. They attached hex dump of header showing bytes: "4150492d4b45593a2031323334...0a" (ends with 0a) -> trailing LF.

alexg: Trailing LF wins. Our API trims whitespace but if there's an extra newline encoded or percent-encoded it can mismatch HMAC / canonicalization. Ask them to base64 of header or raw bytes.

infra-az: Also, if their sidecar uses file-based secret mounted from k8s and the mount had CRLF from Windows commit, that could add \r\n. We saw \r (0d) + \n (0a) problems before.

eli: Quick mitigation: create a temporary api key in the console and set it directly in client to confirm validity. If temporary key works, it's definitely client-side secret munging.

maria-s: Customer tried a console-created temp key -> 200 OK. So it's client-side. They ran `xxd` and saw trailing 0d 0a. They think an older secret rotation script wrote with \r\n.

alexg: Great repro. Root cause: client rotation tool wrote CRLF and Node process didn't trim. Fix options: trim header before send, or ensure secret file sanitized on rotate. We'll add a note in troubleshooting docs about CRLF and MSI caching.

maria-s: Customer fixed rotation script to write without CRLF and restarted pods. Confirmed 200s. :tada:

eli: Action items: 
- alexg to add short KB entry in docs/support about trailing CRLFs & long-running processes (ETA 2 days)
- infra-az to add a checklist item to rotation playbook to restart consumers or use signal/reload (ETA 1d)
- support-bot to close ticket after confirm in 24h

support-bot: Ticket #C-12458 status updated -> resolved (pending verification).

maria-s: Marking resolved on thread, adding note to ticket about MSI cache + CRLF root cause. :thumbsup:
